placements.why: The three segments describe a test built specifically to reproduce a known production failure and check two invariants against it — this is organizational proof-work (validating fixes against real failure modes), not opportunity, strategy, or architecture content. Nothing in the supplied strata (empty) covers this category, so it is minted standalone as the foundational 'Proof' organizational tier.
placements.title: Verification work earns trust through reproducible test guarantees
placements.frame: What must a regression test guarantee to count as proof against a known production failure?

placements.title: Reproducing a production failure becomes the proof surface for its fix
placements.frame: What invariants must hold when a test reproduces this specific production failure pattern?
placements.why: src-1 names the reproduction target (prod's missing-id pattern: a markdown heading with no id field); src-2 and src-3 state the two guarantees the test exists to check against that reproduction — no crash, and a valid slug produced. Together these are a directional theme future test envelopes will keep feeding (more reproduced failure patterns, more invariants checked), not a one-time fact — the grain test admits it as a leaf. No existing narrative leaf was supplied to reuse, so it mints under the newly-minted Proof strata.
